title: Research Methods in Education
topics: Nature and purpose of educational research

items.q: Confidentiality may be defined as
o: the keeping of personal information from being disclosed to others
the entire group to which the findings are meant to apply
use of whatever cases happen to be at hand
a written set of items to which a respondent supplies answers without the researcher's help
items.s: Confidentiality: the keeping of personal information from being disclosed to others. The other options describe Convenience sampling, Target population, Questionnaire.

items.q: The statement “inquiry that seeks the causes of an observed state of affairs” describes which of the following?
o: Applied research
Empirical evidence
Explanatory research
Educational research
items.s: Explanatory research is inquiry that seeks the causes of an observed state of affairs.
items.t: Nature and purpose of educational research

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Case study design.

techniques that allow conclusions about a population from sample data
an intensive study of one pupil, class or school taken as a single unit
a set of tasks used to measure what a learner has gained from instruction

items.q: Random sampling may be defined as
o: the extent to which scores behave as the underlying idea of the trait predicts

the degree to which an instrument measures what it claims to measure

items.q: Which of the following best describes Null hypothesis?

the orderly search for new knowledge by gathering and interpreting evidence
knowledge resting on observation or measurement rather than on opinion
a small trial of the whole procedure carried out before the main fieldwork

items.q: The statement “the boundaries that mark what the inquiry did and did not cover” describes which of the following?

the admitted weakness in design or data that qualifies the results
the degree to which an instrument measures what it claims to measure

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Random sampling?

the quality of a measure that gives the same result whoever applies it

the formal permission obtained from the appropriate body before data collection begins
the keeping of personal information from being disclosed to others
the presentation of another writer's work or ideas as one's own
items.s: Confidentiality: the keeping of personal information from being disclosed to others. The other options describe Ethical clearance, Plagiarism, Non-response.

items.q: The correct meaning of Research proposal is
o: the written statement of the problem, plan and budget submitted before the study starts
the formal permission obtained from the appropriate body before data collection begins
the stage of going to the school or setting to collect the data in person
the keeping of personal information from being disclosed to others
items.s: Research proposal: the written statement of the problem, plan and budget submitted before the study starts. The other options describe Confidentiality, Fieldwork, Ethical clearance.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the body of accepted ideas that gives the study its point of view”
o: Primary source
Theoretical framework
Literature review
Null hypothesis
items.s: Theoretical framework is the body of accepted ideas that gives the study its point of view.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Pilot study?
o: a guided conversation among a small group on one topic
a measure taken before the treatment is applied
a spoken exchange in which the researcher asks and records answers
a small trial of the whole procedure carried out before the main fieldwork

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Unstructured interview.

a small trial of the whole procedure carried out before the main fieldwork
a guided conversation among a small group on one topic

items.q: Interpretation of findings may be defined as
o: information in the form of words, images or description rather than numbers
the small probability, usually five in a hundred, at which a result is accepted as real
the organisation and treatment of collected information so that it yields answers
the explanation of what the analysis means in relation to the questions asked

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Variable.
o: a hidden factor lying between cause and effect that cannot be directly seen
the holding constant of conditions so that their effect does not enter the result
a quality or quantity that can take different values among the cases studied
a factor that alters the strength of the link between two others
items.s: Variable: a quality or quantity that can take different values among the cases studied. The other options describe Moderating variable, Control, Intervening variable.

items.q: The correct meaning of Independent variable is
o: a quality or quantity that can take different values among the cases studied
the factor that the researcher manipulates or treats as the cause
a factor that alters the strength of the link between two others
the holding constant of conditions so that their effect does not enter the result
items.s: Independent variable: the factor that the researcher manipulates or treats as the cause. The other options describe Control, Moderating variable, Variable.

items.q: In this course, Construct validity refers to
o: the degree to which findings from a natural setting are credible and confirmable
the extent to which scores behave as the underlying idea of the trait predicts
the use of more than one source, method or researcher to check a finding
the consistency of an instrument in producing the same result on repetition
items.s: Construct validity: the extent to which scores behave as the underlying idea of the trait predicts. The other options describe Trustworthiness of qualitative data, Triangulation, Reliability.

items.q: In this course, Purposive sampling refers to
o: deliberate choice of cases judged best able to answer the question
the procedure of selecting cases from a population in a principled way
use of whatever cases happen to be at hand
the entire group to which the findings are meant to apply

a spoken exchange in which the researcher asks and records answers
a free conversation guided only by the broad aim of the study
the watching and recording of behaviour as it actually occurs
items.s: Unstructured interview: a free conversation guided only by the broad aim of the study. The other options describe Achievement test, Interview, Observation.

items.q: Document analysis may be defined as

a guided conversation among a small group on one topic
a free conversation guided only by the broad aim of the study
the examination of existing records such as registers and minutes for evidence

items.q: The correct meaning of Alternative hypothesis is
o: a precise question the study is designed to answer
the gap in knowledge that the study sets out to close
the organised survey of what has already been written on a problem
the prediction that a difference or relationship does exist

items.q: In this course, Triangulation refers to

the degree to which findings from a natural setting are credible and confirmable
the use of more than one source, method or researcher to check a finding
the consistency of an instrument in producing the same result on repetition

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Anonymity.
o: the failure of those selected to return or give the required data
the removal of names so that no response can be traced to a person
the keeping of personal information from being disclosed to others
the presentation of another writer's work or ideas as one's own

items.q: Target population may be defined as

the entire group to which the findings are meant to apply
the difference between what a sample shows and what the whole population would show
use of whatever cases happen to be at hand

Target population
Sample
Stratified sampling

o: Stratified sampling
Target population
Random sampling
Purposive sampling

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the difference between what a sample shows and what the whole population would show”
o: Convenience sampling
Sampling error
Random sampling
Target population
items.s: Sampling error is the difference between what a sample shows and what the whole population would show.

items.q: The correct meaning of Action research is
o: knowledge resting on observation or measurement rather than on opinion
inquiry carried out by a teacher in the classroom in order to improve that practice
the orderly search for new knowledge by gathering and interpreting evidence
inquiry that seeks the causes of an observed state of affairs
items.s: Action research: inquiry carried out by a teacher in the classroom in order to improve that practice. The other options describe Empirical evidence, Research, Explanatory research.

items.q: Recommendation may be defined as
o: the judgement drawn about the problem, supported by the evidence presented
the short opening summary that states the problem, method and main findings
the suggestion for what practitioners or policy makers should do on the strength of the results
the list of every work referred to in the body of the report

items.q: Case study design may be defined as
o: an intensive study of one pupil, class or school taken as a single unit
a plan in which the cause is applied and its effect observed under controlled conditions
the study of a sample selected from a population in order to describe that population
inquiry in which the presumed cause has already operated and is only examined afterwards
items.s: Case study design: an intensive study of one pupil, class or school taken as a single unit. The other options describe Survey design, Experimental design, Ex post facto design.

items.q: The correct meaning of Content validity is
o: the degree to which findings from a natural setting are credible and confirmable
an index of internal consistency calculated from the responses to all items at once
the degree to which the items cover the whole of what the test should cover
the degree to which an instrument measures what it claims to measure
items.s: Content validity: the degree to which the items cover the whole of what the test should cover. The other options describe Cronbach alpha, Validity, Trustworthiness of qualitative data.

items.q: Continuous variable may be defined as
o: the statement of how a quality will be measured or observed in the study
the factor that the researcher manipulates or treats as the cause
a factor that alters the strength of the link between two others
a quantity that can take any value within a range
items.s: Continuous variable: a quantity that can take any value within a range. The other options describe Moderating variable, Operational definition, Independent variable.

items.q: The correct meaning of Quantitative data is
o: the explanation of what the analysis means in relation to the questions asked
information expressed in numbers that can be counted or measured
the naming of segments of raw information with brief labels so that they can be grouped
techniques that allow conclusions about a population from sample data
items.s: Quantitative data: information expressed in numbers that can be counted or measured. The other options describe Inferential statistics, Interpretation of findings, Coding.

items.q: The correct meaning of Moderating variable is
o: a quantity that can take any value within a range
a quality or quantity that can take different values among the cases studied
a factor that alters the strength of the link between two others
a hidden factor lying between cause and effect that cannot be directly seen
items.s: Moderating variable: a factor that alters the strength of the link between two others. The other options describe Continuous variable, Variable, Intervening variable.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the organised statement of what the data revealed”
o: Findings
Abstract
Scope of the study
Referencing style
items.s: Findings is the organised statement of what the data revealed.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Explanatory research?
o: inquiry undertaken to extend understanding of a phenomenon without immediate practical use
knowledge resting on observation or measurement rather than on opinion
inquiry that seeks the causes of an observed state of affairs
inquiry carried out by a teacher in the classroom in order to improve that practice

items.q: “a statement that there is no real difference or relationship between the variables” is the definition of
o: Research question
Primary source
Null hypothesis
Hypothesis
items.s: Null hypothesis is a statement that there is no real difference or relationship between the variables.

the procedure of selecting cases from a population in a principled way
selection of whole groups such as classes or schools rather than of individuals
deliberate choice of cases judged best able to answer the question

inquiry in which the presumed cause has already operated and is only examined afterwards
an intensive study of one pupil, class or school taken as a single unit
a plan using existing groups because learners cannot be assigned at random

o: a testable statement about the expected relationship between variables
the prediction that a difference or relationship does exist
the organised survey of what has already been written on a problem
a report written by the person who actually carried out the study

a factor that alters the strength of the link between two others
the holding constant of conditions so that their effect does not enter the result

a measure taken before the treatment is applied
a small trial of the whole procedure carried out before the main fieldwork
a written set of items to which a respondent supplies answers without the researcher's help

knowledge resting on observation or measurement rather than on opinion
inquiry undertaken to solve a concrete problem of practice
inquiry that seeks the causes of an observed state of affairs

the degree to which findings from a natural setting are credible and confirmable
the consistency of an instrument in producing the same result on repetition

Observation
Questionnaire
Pilot study

the agreement of participants after they have understood what the study entails
the formal permission obtained from the appropriate body before data collection begins

inquiry undertaken to solve a concrete problem of practice
